what_was_found: During the round itself: a closed verification window's in-progress flows carried on through the established accept, unmetered (a 3 MB cap let 8 MB through); fixed with a conntrack mark.
The pre-auth DNS limiter sat after the established accept, so a client's UDP socket was metered only until the first reply; fixed by moving both limiters before it.
The netd boot reconcile replayed the stored unbound fragment, so new resolver settings waited for a network change; boot now renders it from the current renderer.

The Stripe adapter could never create a checkout on a Managed Payments account (the default for new accounts) because it always sent payment_method_types; fixed with card-only variants under their own idempotency keys.
Correction of the previous round: guest IPv6 was already dropped (meta nfproto ipv6); the earlier count missed that form.
delivered: Temporary internet while reading the code (migration 0111): after an email code is issued and sent, a timed, quota-capped, rate-policed WAN-only window for the requesting device, separate from every entitlement; defaults 10 min, 2/1 Mbps, 25 MB, 3 per device and per address per 24 h, 50 at once; persisted, bounded, audited settings; one live window per device; restore after restart with what is left.
Guest IPv6 guard extended to the return path, before the established accept, counted.
DNS: pre-auth devices 20 qps per address (burst 40) on gateway and public resolvers, counted; unbound ip-ratelimit 100, ratelimit 1000, deny-any.
OTP: issue refused without a kernel-resolved device; verification fails closed without a matching binding; query strings never logged; the link page sends no Referer and is not indexed.

Provider-managed conversion (migration 0112): Stripe accounts may be marked provider-converts (audited, step-up; Paymob refused); presentment kept; the provider settlement report recorded once; shown in Settlements; no local FX; room charge unchanged.
